# Artifact Keeper 1.7.8

A patch release on the 1.7 line with **one data-loss fix you should read before upgrading**, security updates to the bundled scanner binaries, one security fix, and a reporting fix. No schema migrations.

> **1.7.7 was never released.** The tag exists but no images and no release object were ever published — its publish failed on the scanner CVEs described below, and the tag could not be recut because release tags are immutable. 1.7.8 supersedes it and contains everything 1.7.7 would have shipped. If you are on 1.7.6, upgrade straight to 1.7.8. See #3466.

## Read this first — Maven storage GC could delete hand-repaired objects

If you have ever repaired a Maven 404 by inserting a row into `maven_flat_object_owner`, **that object may already be gone**.

Since 1.7.0 the orphan Maven flat-object sweep enumerated its delete candidates from `maven_flat_object_owner` and tested only catalog anchors. But an owner row is also what makes a legacy row-less object *readable*, and inserting one is the documented remediation for keys the catalog-only backfill cannot see. For exactly that class every arm of the predicate was true by construction and permanently, so **the row that made an object servable was the row that queued it for deletion**. An operator who fixed a fail-closed 404 by attributing the key got a 200 for one hour, then lost the bytes.

**Two changes close it:**

1. The sweep now reclaims only rows the system wrote and can re-derive — `primary_row`, `metadata_files`, `derived_checksum`, `metadata_rollup`, `write_claim`. An operator-inserted row is a primary record, and **any source value the system does not write is now protected**.
2. The sweep is **opt-in**, behind `MAVEN_FLAT_GC_ENABLED`. Unset, it reports what it would reclaim and deletes nothing — matching the OCI blob sweep's posture of biasing toward leaking storage over losing data.

**Affected versions:** 1.7.0 through 1.8.0 — treat every release in that range as equally affected. The sweep has enumerated its candidates from `maven_flat_object_owner` since 1.7.0, runs on the hourly scheduled pass, and reclaims up to 1000 keys per pass on every replica that runs the tick. **Do not use your version to rule yourself out:** if you have ever hand-attributed a Maven key on any 1.7.x release, check.

**If you may be affected:** there is no recovery from within Artifact Keeper — the sweep hard-deletes the object and its attribution row together, with no tombstone or journal. Recovery depends on storage-side retention: object versioning, a lifecycle noncurrent window, a bucket replica, or a filesystem backup. Each reclaim emitted `Storage GC: reclaimed orphaned row-less Maven flat object` at INFO with the `storage_key`, so a backend log with sufficient retention reconstructs the key list to restore from.

The same fix ships on the current line as **1.8.1**.

## Security — bundled scanner binaries

The vulnerability scanners shipped inside our images carried known-vulnerable Go dependencies. These are **CVEs in bundled third-party tooling, not in Artifact Keeper's own code**, and none is reachable through the Artifact Keeper API.

- **`usr/local/bin/trivy`** in the scanner-adapter image: 10 HIGH cleared. Six are Go stdlib against the go1.26.5 build (`CVE-2026-33818`, `-56853`, `-56858`, `-56859`, `-56860`, `-56862`), two are `golang.org/x/net` (`CVE-2026-39821`, `CVE-2026-46600`), and two are `golang.org/x/mod` (`CVE-2026-56864`, `CVE-2026-56865`). The adapter now bundles a rebuild of upstream Trivy v0.74.0 on go1.26.7, which pins `x/mod` v0.40.0 itself, and all ten clear at the source. Two of the ten — `CVE-2026-39821` and `CVE-2026-46600` — were suppressed in this branch's `.trivyignore`, so the publish gate only ever saw eight of them; they were present in the shipped binary either way and are gone now.
- **`usr/local/bin/scanner-adapter`**, the adapter's own binary: the published 1.2.3 image was built before go1.26.6 existed and carried the same six Go-stdlib HIGHs. The rebuilt scanner-adapter image, published as **1.2.6**, scans clean on both binaries.
- **`usr/local/bin/grype`** in the backend image: the same `x/mod` pair cleared, by overriding the module to v0.40.0 in the build. No upstream Grype release carries this bump — v0.117.0 is the newest release and even Grype's `main` still pins v0.38.0 — so an explicit override was the only source-level fix available.

**On severity, honestly:** both `x/mod` advisories are scoped to `x/mod/sumdb` and `sumdb/tlog`, and neither package is linked into the Grype binary at all — Grype parses Go binaries, it does not fetch modules. Trivy reports at module granularity from Go build info, so it flags the dependency version regardless of whether the vulnerable code is reachable. We fixed at the source rather than suppressing, but no Artifact Keeper deployment was exploitable through this.

Both image build stages now assert a minimum Go toolchain patch, so a floating base tag cannot silently reintroduce stdlib advisories the way it did here.

## Security

**RUSTSEC-2026-0258** — the bundled `h2` HTTP/2 implementation is updated from 0.4.13 to 0.4.16, closing an unbounded-empty-DATA-frame denial of service. Worth taking promptly on any instance whose gRPC port is reachable from an untrusted network: `tonic` serves h2c only, so the frame decoder is reached **before any application authentication runs**. Upstream rates it Low — the frames are empty, so an attacker trades bandwidth for per-frame bookkeeping rather than payload.

## Fixed

**Proxied downloads are counted again** for Docker/OCI, cargo, NuGet, Debian, Helm and Go, joining the formats that already recorded them. A class-level guard now fails the build if a new proxy serve path records nothing without an explicit marker.

Note that surfacing those counts in the artifact listing arrived in 1.8.0 and is **not** on this line, so 1.7.8 records the data without displaying it in that view. Upgrading to 1.8.1 shows the counts, with the history recorded from this release onward intact.
